title: Morphisms correspond to clopen graphs projecting isomorphically
statement: Let $p:U\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $q:V\to Y$ a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Put $P=V\times_Y U$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projection $r:P\to U$. There exists a bijection from the set of morphisms $a:U\to V$ satisfying $q\circ a=p$ to the set of open subsets $W\subseteq P$ [def-weil-open-immersion] that are also closed and for which $r|_W$ is an isomorphism. The underlying subset assigned to $a$ is the image of its graph $(a,\mathrm{id}_U):U\to P$.

proof.text: The graph is a section of the finite etale projection. A section is an open and closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. Its inverse on its open image is the restricted projection, so it gives the stated clopen.

An open immersion is isomorphic to the open subscheme of its image (Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Restrict.lean:423). This identifies the inverse of that isomorphism with the restricted projection by composing with the graph and using its section identity. Conversely the inverse of r|_W followed by W inclusion is a section; compose it with the first product projection to obtain a over Y. The pullback identities verify the required triangle. This is the explicit inverse construction.

To check uniqueness, equal graph images give an isomorphism between the two graph domains (IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq, OpenImmersion.lean:727). Composing its factorization equality with r identifies the isomorphism with the identity, so the two graphs and then their first projections coincide. To check surjectivity, the graph constructed from W is the inverse of its projection followed by W inclusion; its image is W because that inverse is surjective. These are the hinj and hsurj computations in the delivered proof.
